title: Arbitration and Dispute Resolution
overview: Effective dispute resolution minimizes costs and preserves relationships often strained by commercial disputes. When informal negotiations fail, mediation or arbitration frequently provides a practical alternative to litigation. This course offers participants a lawyer’s perspective on dispute resolution, emphasizing arbitration as a preferred method to avoid court proceedings. Attendees will gain a comprehensive understanding of various dispute resolution techniques and learn to apply them to reduce the risk of litigation.
audience: This course is designed for professionals across various industries involved in contract management and dispute resolution, including project managers, contract managers, procurement managers, supply chain managers, contractors, architects, developers, and engineers. It is especially beneficial for in-house counsel and legal advisors new to the GCC who require a foundational understanding of regional dispute resolution practices.
methodology: This highly interactive course features exercises, case studies, and group discussions. Participants will collaborate in pairs and larger groups to analyze regional and international dispute resolution scenarios.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Determine the most appropriate approach to resolving legal disputes.
Minimize the likelihood of disputes escalating to litigation.
Apply local and international legal frameworks for dispute resolution.
Utilize arbitration principles to negotiate favorable terms.
Leverage case law to secure advantageous outcomes for their organization.
